text: Writing clean code is a vital skill for any programmer. At its heart, it is about making your code readable for humans, not just computers. This starts with clear naming conventions; for instance, a variable like `userAge` is much better than `x`. More importantly, clean code relies on breaking down problems into small, focused functions. Each function should do one thing well, making it easier to test. This focus on readability and structure leads to better maintainability, meaning you and others can easily update fix bugs without breaking everything. Ultimately, clean code saves time and avoids frustration for everyone involved.
